explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose
   - This is a Go-based, cross-platform, terminal CLI tool (“tgpt”) that lets users interact with AI text/chat providers and image-generation providers from their shell.
   - The README describes installation, available AI/image providers, proxy support, and general usage—confirming it’s a full-featured CLI application with a plugin-style architecture for different back-end services.

2. Analyze the file structure
   - Top-level files
     • main.go: CLI entrypoint and command dispatch  
     • go.mod/go.sum, build.sh, install scripts, LICENSE, README  
   - Directories under src/
     • bubbletea: UI layer (TUI using bubbletea framework)  
     • client: core HTTP client and orchestration logic  
     • helper, utils: miscellaneous helper functions/utilities  
     • structs: shared data-type definitions (requests, responses)  
     • providers: registry and per-provider implementations for text/chat  
     • imagegen: image generation module and its providers (arta, pollinations)  
   - md/: documentation on providers and usage
   - config files: tgpt.json, version.txt

3. Examine the README for additional insights
   - Emphasizes provider-based design—users can choose from multiple AI or image providers  
   - Proxy support via environment or config file  
   - tUI element (bubbletea) for interactive sessions  
   - No existing architecture diagram, but the README outlines the modules and running flow

4. Main components and interactions to include in your system-design diagram
   a. Components
      1. CLI Entrypoint (main.go & Cobra or flag parsing)
      2. TUI Layer (bubbletea module)
      3. Command/Orchestration Layer (client package)
      4. Provider Registry (providers/providers.go)
      5. Text/Chat Providers (each src/providers/*)
      6. Image Generation Layer (imagegen package + its sub-providers)
      7. Shared Data Models (structs package)
      8. Utilities & Helpers (utils, helper packages)
      9. Configuration Store (proxy.txt, tgpt.json, environment variables)
     10. External HTTP Services (OpenAI, Gemini, Pollinations, etc.)
   b. Relationships & Data Flows
      - User types a command → CLI Entrypoint → passes arguments to TUI or client  
      - TUI calls orchestration layer when needed (e.g., interactive chat)  
      - Orchestration layer consults config (proxy, API keys) → selects appropriate Provider via Provider Registry  
      - Invokes specific Provider implementation → makes HTTP request to external AI/Image service → receives response  
      - Response marshaled into shared structs → passed back up to TUI or printed to stdout  
      - ImageGen module follows similar path for image requests  
   c. Architectural patterns & principles
      - Plugin/Factory pattern for providers: centralized registry dynamically instantiates provider implementations  
      - Layered modular design: UI → Orchestration → Providers → External API  
      - Separation of concerns: Raw HTTP client code isolated in client package, business logic in providers, UI in bubbletea  
      - Configuration abstraction: supports environment variables and config files  
   d. Key technologies/libraries
      - Go modules (go.mod)
      - Bubbletea TUI framework (github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea)
      - HTTP client (net/http under client package)
      - JSON/YAML parsing for config
      - Build & install scripts (build.sh, install-win.ps1)

5. Tailoring the diagram for this CLI application
   - Emphasize the linear flow: CLI entry → command parsing → orchestration → provider invocation → external service → back up to user.  
   - Group all provider implementations under a “Providers” cluster.  
   - Show plugin registration: providers.go registering each concrete provider.  
   - Highlight the TUI layer separately from the non-interactive “print to stdout” path.

6. Diagram guidelines (to include)
   - Clear, concise labels for each component box  
   - Directional arrows showing request flow (user → CLI → orchestration → provider → external API → orchestration → UI → user)  
   - Use color coding or shapes:
     • Blue boxes for internal modules (CLI, client, providers, utils)  
     • Green boxes for external services (OpenAI, Pollinations, etc.)  
     • Orange box for configuration store  
     • Dashed arrows for configuration or control flow (e.g., reading proxy settings)  
   - Annotate critical interfaces, e.g., “ProviderRegistry.Register(providerName, ProviderFunc)”

7. Emphasis
   - Capture all major modules: bubbletea (UI), client (orchestration), providers, imagegen, utils, structs  
   - Don’t overcomplicate—one box per module or logical group, arrows for data flow  
   - Note plugin pattern in the provider layer so new providers can be added seamlessly  
   - Ensure the diagram can be understood by any developer encountering the codebase for the first time  

By following this breakdown, the principal engineer will have a clear roadmap for drawing an accurate, detailed architecture diagram of tgpt’s CLI-based, plugin-driven system.
</explanation>
